text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "Verified against the code: all imports exist (config.settings.feature, eligibility.rules.is_eligible, payments.vouchers.DuplicatePayment/disburse/payment_key, registry.register.load_households). payment_key(household_id, 2) produces the documented idempotency key '{household_id}:cycle' and disburse() raises DuplicatePayment on reuse, so re-runs cannot double-pay. The sys.path insert points to the repo root (scripts/..). The feature-flag check matches feature() in settings.py, and is_eligible already excludes non-active households, so the ValueError path for non-active households in disburse() is only a safety net and won't be hit for the eligible set. Eligibility follows the existing rules (vulnerability score vs threshold, pregnancy-adjusted). The script pays exactly the eligible set, 60 dollars, cycle 2, once each, and writes only via disburse() to data/outbox/payments.jsonl. Nothing existing is broken since this is a new file."}}
reasoning:
Check the script logic. It loads households twice (once for dict, once for eligible set) — fine. is_eligible filters non-active. disburse raises ValueError for non-active households — but eligible set only contains active ones, so fine. DuplicatePayment caught. Feature flag checked first. payment_key format matches. sys.path insert correct (scripts/ parent.parent = repo root). Docstring mentions outbox. All imports exist: config.settings.feature, eligibility.rules.is_eligible, payments.vouchers.DuplicatePayment/disburse/payment_key, registry.register.load_households. All verified.

One subtlety: is_eligible called without `today` — defaults to None, vulnerability_score uses today presumably. That's the "existing pattern" per the plan. Fine.

Accept.
